blocks.title: Activity diagram
blocks.text: Activity diagrams show the flow of activities or steps in a process. They are useful for modelling the logic of complex operations.

Example: in a restaurant management system, an activity diagram can represent the process from order placement to food preparation and finally to order delivery (Fig. 1.12). The process begins at Start, moves to Order Placement, then to Food Preparation; a decision diamond asks whether the food is ready: if yes it goes to Order Delivery, if no to Re-prepare Food and back; the End node concludes the process. Arrows show the sequence, making it easy to follow how an order progresses.

blocks.alt: Flowchart: Start (oval) to Order Placement to Food Preparation to a diamond, Food Ready?. Yes leads right to Order Delivery; No leads left to Re-Prepare Food, which returns up to Food Preparation. Lines from Re-Prepare Food and Order Delivery meet at a small connector circle, from which one arrow goes to End (oval).
